ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A logistics company uses a chute to directly load goods into trucks. The inclined chute makes an angle of $24^{\circ}$ with the horizontal, and has a length $l_{1}=4\mathrm{m}$. The length of the horizontal chute is adjustable, and the two chutes are smoothly connected. The goods slide down from the top of the inclined chute starting from rest. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the goods and the chute is $m=\frac{2}{9}$. The goods can be treated as a point mass (take $\cos24^{\circ}=0.9$, $\sin24^{\circ}=0.4$, and the acceleration due to gravity $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$).

1. Determine the magnitude of the acceleration $a_{1}$ of the goods while sliding on the inclined chute.
2. Determine the magnitude of the velocity $v$ of the goods at the end of the inclined chute.
3. If the velocity of the goods when leaving the end of the horizontal chute does not exceed $2\mathsf{m}/\mathsf{s}$, determine the shortest length $l_{2}$ of the horizontal chute.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, it can be seen that a cargo block is located on the inclined chute at the upper left, and the inclined chute connects downward to the right to a section of horizontal chute; the horizontal chute extends into the upper part of the truck compartment, used to send the cargo directly into the vehicle. The figure marks the angle between the inclined chute and the horizontal dashed line as 24°, and the two sections of chute are smoothly connected. Reasoning calculation: The problem gives the inclined section length l1 = 4 m, the coefficient of kinetic friction μ = 2/9, sin24° = 0.4, cos24° = 0.9, g = 10 m/s², and the cargo begins to slide down from rest. 1. Along the direction of the inclined plane, the component of gravity is mg sin24°, and the magnitude of the friction force is μmg cos24°, so the magnitude of the acceleration is a1 = g(sin24° - μcos24°) = 10[0.4 - (2/9)(0.9)] = 10(0.4 - 0.2) = 2 m/s². 2. Sliding from rest at the top of the inclined plane to the bottom of the inclined plane, use v² = 2a1l1: v² = 2 × 2 × 4 = 16, so v = 4 m/s. 3. After entering the horizontal chute, it is decelerated only by the kinetic friction force in the horizontal direction, and the magnitude of the deceleration is a2 = μg = (2/9) × 10 = 20/9 m/s². It is required that the speed when leaving the horizontal chute not exceed 2 m/s, and the shortest length corresponds to the final speed being exactly 2 m/s. From 2² = 4² - 2(20/9)l2, we get 4 = 16 - (40/9)l2, (40/9)l2 = 12, l2 = 108/40 = 2.7 m.
